title: {{NAME}} and the Cretaceous Cup
moral: Courage is not the absence of surprise, it is acting well in spite of it.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a bright red hero-jersey hybrid with a silver football emblem, dark shorts, and red boots — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The inter-dimensional challenge arrived as a hologram in the middle of {{NAME}}'s training session.

A large, complicated-looking entity with nineteen limbs announced: it would leave the Earth-adjacent dimensions in peace if a representative human team could beat its team at the universal sport.

The universal sport, it turned out, was football.

The entity's team: six creatures with the bodies of Velociraptors but the tactical intelligence of championship players.

"The good news," said {{NAME}}'s team captain, "is that we're good at football."

"The neutral news," said {{NAME}}, "is that so are they."

pages.content:
He studied the entity's team footage for three hours.

Raptor-form meant: fast direction changes, low centre of gravity, three-directional peripheral vision, and a communication system between them that operated faster than human players could signal.

The weakness: they communicated through movement cues. If {{NAME}}'s team's movements were unpredictable, the communication advantage would reduce.

"We play chaos football," he told his team. "Not random. Structured chaos. We have plays, but we don't signal them in advance. We react in real time."

His team looked at him.

"Aren't we always supposed to communicate?" asked someone.

"Not today," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The match was seventy minutes of the most intense football {{NAME}} had ever played.

The Raptor team was extraordinary: faster, stronger, and communicating with a precision that made their defensive shape almost impenetrable.

But the chaos strategy disrupted their prediction models. By the fourth time {{NAME}}'s team made a move the Raptor team hadn't anticipated, their coordination began to show small fractures: a half-second hesitation here, an overrun there.

Half time: one all.

"We're getting to them," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The winning goal came from a sequence none of them had planned.

{{NAME}} lost the ball in midfield. His teammate Anya recovered it and, with three Raptor players closing, passed blindly backward to the only space available.

{{NAME}} turned and found the ball at his feet in exactly the position he'd told his team to always be available for.

One touch. Shot.

The Raptor goalkeeper dove perfectly for the obvious angle.

The ball took a deflection from a divot in the turf and changed direction by six centimetres.

Goal.

pages.content:
The entity accepted the result with a formality that suggested it didn't accept results often.

{{NAME}} watched the Raptor team pass through the inter-dimensional portal. The last one paused at the edge and looked directly at him.

For one long moment, the Raptor held its gaze.

Then it inclined its head: acknowledgement.

{{NAME}} inclined his head in return.

The portal closed.

In bed that night, he thought about the deflection off the divot.

Sometimes the universe helped you. When you were ready for it.
